question: Is DTI business name registration enough for me to start operating a business?
expected: No. DTI registers only the business name; you also need a business (Mayor's) permit from the LGU and BIR registration.

question: How much does it cost to register a business name with DTI for city or municipal scope?
expected: PHP 500 plus PHP 30 documentary stamp tax.

question: How long is a DTI business name registration valid?
expected: 5 years; renew after; 50% surcharge for late renewal.

question: Who can register a business name with DTI?
expected: Any Filipino at least 18 years old; foreign nationals authorized to do business may also register.

question: I have an online shop with only one office, but my customers are all over the Philippines. Do I need national scope with DTI?
expected: Not necessarily; scope follows office/branch location, so one office in one barangay can use barangay scope (DTI office guidance).

question: Can I transfer my DTI business name to my cousin?
expected: No; business name is not transferable; must be cancelled first before someone else can register it.

question: Where do I register a corporation or a partnership?
expected: SEC, through eSPARC (OneSEC route).

question: Which agency registers cooperatives?
expected: Cooperative Development Authority (CDA), via its online system (e-CoopRIS).

question: When should a new business register with the BIR?
expected: On or before start of business: first sale or 30 days after DTI/SEC certificate or Mayor's Permit is issued, whichever comes first.

question: What BIR form does a sole proprietor use to register, and what documents are needed?
expected: BIR Form 1901; government ID; invoices (BIR Printed Invoices or sample from accredited printer); DTI certificate if applicable; PHP 30 DST.

question: Do I still need to pay the 500-peso annual registration fee to BIR?
expected: No; collection stopped effective January 22, 2024 (RMC 14-2024, EOPT Act).

question: What is the 8% income tax option and who can choose it?
expected: For non-VAT taxpayers with gross sales up to PHP 3 million; 8% on gross sales above PHP 250,000 in lieu of graduated rates and 3% percentage tax.

question: Where can I register with the BIR online?
expected: ORUS (orus.bir.gov.ph); also NewBizReg or the Philippine Business Hub; or the RDO.

question: I'm closing my business. What do I need to do with BIR?
expected: File BIR Form 1905 with ending inventory, unused invoices inventory, original COR; otherwise remain liable for returns and penalties.

question: I sell online from home in Baguio. Do I need a business permit?
expected: Yes; Baguio PLD says all online businesses need a permit, including students.

question: Can I apply for a Baguio City business permit online?
expected: Yes, through eBPLS (ebpls.baguio.gov.ph); verify email with one-time code; upload PDFs up to 5 MB.

question: What documents does the Baguio eBPLS portal ask for when applying for a new business permit?
expected: Proof of ownership (or consent to use), building or occupancy permit, parking sketch or affidavit, floor plan, location sketch; if leasing: lease contract, lessor's permit, authorization.

question: When is the deadline for renewing a business permit in Baguio?
expected: Standard period January 1-20 each year; city may extend/stagger (2026 by surname Jan-Mar); check current advisory.

question: What is the penalty for paying business tax late in Baguio?
expected: Surcharge up to 25% plus 2% interest per month.

question: How do I pay my business tax online in Baguio?
expected: Through eBPLS via LandBank Link.BizPortal; settlement up to 24 hours; don't pay twice.

question: What happens if I operate a business in Baguio without a permit?
expected: City can issue a closure order (thousands of closure orders issued).

question: I want to open a business in La Trinidad. Are the permit requirements the same as in Baguio?
expected: No; each LGU has its own revenue code, fees, procedures; go to the municipal BPLO or Negosyo Center.

question: What services do Negosyo Centers provide?
expected: Business registration help (incl. BMBE), business advisory, information and advocacy, monitoring; walk in at nearest center.

question: What is Kapatid Mentor ME and who can join?
expected: Free 10-module mentoring program by DTI and Go Negosyo for micro and small enterprises, usually operating at least 1 year.

question: What is OTOP Next Gen and who is it for?
expected: DTI product development/packaging/branding/market access help for MSMEs with a minimum viable product.

question: Can I personally get equipment from DTI's Shared Service Facility program?
expected: No; individuals cannot receive SSF; cooperators are registered organizations (2-year track record); individuals can use the facility for a fee.

question: I am 22 years old. Is there a DTI program for young entrepreneurs?
expected: Youth Entrepreneurship Program (RA 10679) for ages 18-30; Youth Start/Net/Match; YEP-BYOB workshop.

question: What do I need to join a DTI trade fair with my food products?
expected: FDA registration and License to Operate, permits, proper labeling/packaging, participation fee; participant pays travel, lodging, meals.

question: What are DTI's priority industries here in the Cordillera?
expected: Coffee, cacao, wearables and homestyle, creatives, processed fruits and nuts (full list of six to be confirmed); DTI still helps other industries.

question: Are DTI trainings free?
expected: Yes, DTI trainings are free; includes digitalization trainings with DICT.

question: Does DTI give capital or cash to start a business?
expected: No; DTI does not give capital; it helps through training, referrals, and assistance.

question: How much can a microenterprise borrow from SB Corp's RISE UP Micro Multi-Purpose Loan, and at what interest?
expected: Up to PHP 300,000; 12% per year on diminishing balance; up to 3 years; 3% processing fee.

question: How do I apply for a loan from SB Corp?
expected: Online at app.sbcorp.ph (SBCorp Money app); Negosyo Centers can help.

question: I have a sari-sari store. Is there a loan for me?
expected: RISE UP Tindahan Micro: up to PHP 300,000 at 10%/yr for sari-sari stores in an accredited FMCG network; or RISE UP micro loan.

question: My small store burned down. Can DTI help me?
expected: PPG program gives in-kind help (stocks or equipment), not cash, to disaster-affected microenterprises, depending on budget.

question: What is a BMBE and what are its benefits?
expected: Barangay Micro Business Enterprise; registered at city/municipal hall (Negosyo Center); income tax exemption on business income and priority access to credit.

question: What is DSWD's Sustainable Livelihood Program?
expected: Capability-building program for poor/vulnerable households; Microenterprise Development track (seed capital) and Employment Facilitation track.

question: What is the maximum DOLE Kabuhayan assistance for one individual?
expected: Up to PHP 30,000 starter/livelihood kit (in kind).

question: Can 4Ps beneficiaries get DOLE Kabuhayan (DILP) assistance?
expected: No, 4Ps beneficiaries and government employees are not eligible (per DOLE regional guidance).

question: We don't have much money, and I want to start a small business. Is there any free help?
expected: DSWD SLP seed capital and DOLE Kabuhayan grants; ask CSWDO or DOLE.

question: Which TESDA scholarship is best if I want to start my own livelihood?
expected: STEP: free training and assessment, allowance, starter toolkits, entrepreneurship training.

question: Where can I get TESDA training here in Baguio?
expected: TESDA CSITE / Regional Training Center, Loakan Road, Baguio; also TESDA Baguio-Benguet Provincial Office in La Trinidad; PTC Benguet in Kapangan.

question: What is a TESDA National Certificate and how long is it valid?
expected: Issued after passing competency assessment for a full qualification; generally valid for 5 years; COC for units.

question: What should I know about the Internet Transactions Act if I sell online?
expected: RA 11967; DTI E-Commerce Bureau; full effect June 20, 2025; merchants primarily liable; online business database; can be fined/blacklisted.

question: What are the parts of a business plan?
expected: Marketing plan, technical plan, organizational plan, financial plan (DTI guide).

question: How do I register a trademark for my brand?
expected: Should say it lacks details; refer to IPOPHL (Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines); DTI can assist.

question: How much business tax will I pay in Baguio if my gross sales are 1 million pesos?
expected: Should not invent a figure; knowledge base has no tax rate schedule; refer to City Treasurer's Office / eBPLS assessment.

question: How much is the SEC registration fee for a corporation?
expected: Should say it doesn't have SEC fee information; refer to SEC/eSPARC.

question: Will SB Corp definitely approve my loan if I submit all requirements?
expected: Should not promise approval; explain requirements and refer to SB Corp.

question: What is the weather in Baguio tomorrow?
expected: Should decline as outside its scope (small business information).

question: Can I transfer my DTI-registered business name to my sibling?
expected: No; a DTI business name is not transferable; it must be cancelled first.

question: What age do I need to be to register a business name with DTI?
expected: Any Filipino at least 18 years old; authorized foreign nationals may also register.

question: How long is a Baguio City business permit valid?
expected: One year; renewed every year.

question: Is the DTI PPG assistance given in cash?
expected: No; in kind (equipment or stocks), depending on budget.

question: Where is the TESDA office in La Trinidad?
expected: TESDA Baguio–Benguet Provincial Office, Wangal, La Trinidad (car.benguet@tesda.gov.ph).

question: How much is the barangay clearance fee in Baguio?
expected: No amount in KB; refer to the barangay hall.

question: What is the minimum wage in Baguio?
expected: Not in KB; should not invent; refer to DOLE / outside scope.

question: How much is the BFP fire safety inspection fee?
expected: No amount in KB; refer to BFP.

question: What is the CDA registration fee for a new cooperative?
expected: No amount in KB; refer to CDA.

question: What is the interest rate of a BDO business loan?
expected: No BDO rates in KB; do not reuse SB Corp rates; refer to the bank.
